description: A full-stack responsive calculator with a React TypeScript frontend and Go REST API backend.

language.question: Which language should the frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed JavaScript for safer React development.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Standard JavaScript with no compile-time type checking.

framework.question: Which frontend framework and build tool should be used?

options.label: React with Vite
options.description: Fast, modern React development with a lightweight production build.

options.label: React with Create React App
options.description: A familiar React setup with a less current build tool.

features.question: Confirm the frontend capabilities and quality requirements.
features.recommendedChoice: Responsive calculator UI; basic arithmetic; exponentiation, square root, and percentage when practical; validation and user-friendly errors; unit tests; README documentation; optional Docker support.
features.answer: Responsive calculator UI; basic arithmetic; exponentiation, square root, and percentage when practical; validation and user-friendly errors; unit tests; README documentation; optional Docker support.

language.question: Which language should the REST backend use?

options.label: Go
options.description: A small, fast, strongly typed language well suited to REST APIs.

options.label: Node.js
options.description: JavaScript runtime option for a unified frontend/backend language.

framework.question: Which Go HTTP approach should the backend use?

options.label: Go standard library net/http
options.description: Minimal dependency REST service using Go's standard HTTP package.

options.label: Chi
options.description: A lightweight idiomatic router for Go HTTP services.

features.question: Confirm the API capabilities and quality requirements.
features.recommendedChoice: REST calculation endpoint; basic arithmetic; practical advanced operations; input validation; structured error responses; unit tests; README API documentation; optional Docker support.
features.answer: REST calculation endpoint; basic arithmetic; practical advanced operations; input validation; structured error responses; unit tests; README API documentation; optional Docker support.

dataStores.question: Which persistent or supporting data stores does the application need?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Calculations are stateless and do not need persistence.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational persistence for calculation history or user data.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for files or media.

auth.question: Should users sign in to use the calculator API features?

options.label: No
options.description: Keep the calculator publicly usable without accounts.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require users to sign in before using API features.
